name: Students chronically absent (%)
plain: The share of students who missed 15 or more school days in the year, for any reason.
definition: Students absent 15 or more school days in the year, for any reason (excused or not), as a share of the students enrolled. Public schools that answered the Civil Rights Data Collection, placed in a municipio by the NCES school directory; the share is pooled over the schools that report both figures, never an average of school shares. The year is the school year that starts in it (2021 = 2021-22); 2019-20 was not collected.

coverage.frequency: Every two years (2019-20 not collected); school years 2017-18 and 2021-22.

method: school_conditions.py reads the all-students rows of the Civil Rights Data Collection for Puerto Rico's public schools, places each school in a municipio by its NCES id in the Common Core of Data directory of the same year, and pools: a municipio's share is the sum of its schools' numerators over the sum of their denominators, over the schools that report both. Negative codes (missing, not applicable, suppressed) are no value.
source_detail: US Department of Education, Civil Rights Data Collection 2017-18 and 2021-22, public schools, via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal; pooled by municipio
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 8.9% in 2017-18 and 45.7% in 2021-22, the first year back in school buildings after the pandemic. Lowest in 2021-22: Guaynabo (11.2), Aibonito (12.7), San Juan (20); highest: Las Marías (83.2), Aguadilla (81), San Sebastián (77.6).
caveats: Schools report their own figures; the Office for Civil Rights does not audit them, and how a school counts an absence or a part-time staff member can differ.
Differences this large between neighboring municipios may come partly from how each education region recorded absences: read neighbors together.
Check: the Annie E. Casey Foundation's 2024 KIDS COUNT release for Puerto Rico reports 48% of public school students chronically absent around 2022-23.
2017-18 was the school year of Hurricane María; schools that did not reopen are not in it.

name: Students per school counselor
plain: How many students there are for each full-time school counselor.
definition: Students enrolled for each full-time school counselor (full-time equivalents). Puerto Rico's staff items are missing in 2017-18. Public schools that answered the Civil Rights Data Collection, placed in a municipio by the NCES school directory; the share is pooled over the schools that report both figures, never an average of school shares. The year is the school year that starts in it (2021 = 2021-22); 2019-20 was not collected.

coverage.frequency: Every two years (2019-20 not collected); school years 2017-18 and 2021-22.

method: school_conditions.py reads the all-students rows of the Civil Rights Data Collection for Puerto Rico's public schools, places each school in a municipio by its NCES id in the Common Core of Data directory of the same year, and pools: a municipio's share is the sum of its schools' numerators over the sum of their denominators, over the schools that report both. Negative codes (missing, not applicable, suppressed) are no value.
source_detail: US Department of Education, Civil Rights Data Collection 2017-18 and 2021-22, public schools, via the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal; pooled by municipio
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 546 students per counselor in 2021-22. Fewest: Maricao (201), Aibonito (344), Utuado (345); most: Trujillo Alto (3206), Cataño (1923), Sabana Grande (1832).
caveats: Schools report their own figures; the Office for Civil Rights does not audit them, and how a school counts an absence or a part-time staff member can differ.
Puerto Rico's staff items are missing in the 2017-18 collection, so the staff measures have 2021-22 only.
A municipio whose schools report no counselor has no value, not an infinite ratio; see the share of schools with no counselor.
